name: Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary
tagline: Forty-odd rhododendron species on the road to Yumthang
meta_description: Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary, North Sikkim: bloom months, species, birds, how to see it from Lachung on the Yumthang road, permits and conservation rules.
summary: Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary covers about 43 sq km of the Lachung valley between Lachung and Yumthang, at roughly 3,000–3,700 m. Created in 1984, it protects two to four dozen rhododendron species, including Sikkim's state tree. You see it from the Yumthang road; the bloom peaks from late April to May.
intro: Most people drive through Shingba without knowing its name. The road from Lachung to Yumthang climbs for about 24 km through forest of fir, birch and rhododendron, and for much of that distance you are inside the Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary. It was declared in 1984 and covers about 43 square km of the upper Lachung valley, roughly between 3,000 and 3,700 m.

The sanctuary exists for one family of plants. Sources count anything from about 24 to 40 species of rhododendron here, from trees several metres tall to small shrubs. Sikkim's state tree, Rhododendron niveum, with its magenta flower heads, grows in this altitude band. In spring the slopes turn red, pink, white, yellow and mauve, with peak bloom usually from late April to mid-May.

Shingba is also good for birds and is part of the wider Sacred Himalayan Landscape conservation area. Recorded species include the wood snipe and the hoary-throated barwing. You visit on your Lachung permit as part of the Yumthang morning; there is no separate walking route for tourists, but short, careful stops along the road show you a great deal.

story.title: A sanctuary for a single family of trees
paras: When Joseph Hooker came up these valleys in 1849, he found rhododendrons in more forms than any European had seen: tree-sized and shrub-sized, scarlet, white, yellow, purple. His illustrated folio, The Rhododendrons of Sikkim-Himalaya, published between 1849 and 1851, and the seed he sent to Kew, helped make the rhododendron a fixture of British gardens.

More than a century later, Sikkim set aside part of the Lachung valley to protect these forests from cutting and grazing pressure. The Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary was established in 1984 with an area of about 43 square km. The state also chose Rhododendron niveum as its state tree, a species native to Sikkim, Bhutan and southern Tibet that grows between about 2,600 and 3,500 m.

The sanctuary sits inside a working landscape. Lachung villagers still take animals up to Yumthang in summer, and the Lachung Dzumsa manages its own community forests below. The pressure today comes mostly from roads and tourism. Staying on the road edge, carrying out your waste and never breaking a branch is your part of keeping it intact.
story.source: Wikipedia, 'Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary', 'Mangan district', 'Rhododendron niveum' and 'Joseph Dalton Hooker'

did_you_know: The Shingba sanctuary was established in 1984 and covers about 43 square km of the Lachung valley.
Rhododendron niveum, Sikkim's state tree, has leaves with a white felt underneath and magenta to lilac flowers held in a tight ball.
The hoary-throated barwing and wood snipe are among the birds recorded in the sanctuary.

highlights.title: Spring bloom
highlights.text: From about the third week of April to late May, rhododendrons flower through the sanctuary, lower slopes first and higher ones later. Early mornings on the Yumthang road are the best time to see and photograph them.

highlights.title: The state tree
highlights.text: Look for Rhododendron niveum, with compact balls of magenta or lilac flowers and leaves white-felted underneath. Ask your driver or a local guide to point it out; it grows in this altitude band.

highlights.title: Fir and birch forest
highlights.text: Between the rhododendrons, the sanctuary holds tall silver fir and birch, draped with lichen. On misty mornings the forest is quiet and atmospheric, even outside flower season.

highlights.title: High-altitude birds
highlights.text: Shingba's recorded birds include the hoary-throated barwing and wood snipe. Pheasants such as the blood pheasant are found in similar forests in Sikkim. Early mornings and binoculars give you the best chance.

highlights.title: Autumn and winter faces
highlights.text: In October and November the forest turns gold and russet; from December the road is often under snow. The sanctuary is never closed to the Yumthang drive when the road is open, but flowers are a spring event.

how_to_reach.text: Every Lachung group package's Yumthang morning passes through the sanctuary. Ask your driver for one or two short stops on the way up. Packages cost about ₹3,500–5,500 per person for one night from Gangtok, indicative, 2026.

With a private car you can take the Yumthang road more slowly, leaving Lachung at first light and stopping several times. The cost is part of your Lachung car hire, about ₹9,000–13,000 for 1N/2D from Gangtok, indicative, 2026.

The nearest airport is Bagdogra (IXB) and the railhead NJP. Go to Gangtok, then Lachung, and enter the sanctuary on the Yumthang road the next morning. Permits through a registered operator are required.

where_to_stay: There is no accommodation inside the sanctuary. Stay in Lachung, a short drive below. Budget travellers can try a family homestay such as Bichu Homestay; Le Coxy Resort is a solid comfort option with heated mattresses; and Yarlam Resort, on the hillside above Lachung amid fir and rhododendron, is the premium choice. Book early for late April and May, the busiest weeks of the year in Lachung.
budget_tip: Travel in the last week of April instead of mid-May; the bloom is usually well under way and Lachung hotel rates have not yet hit their peak.
tips: Leave Lachung at 5.30–6 am for the best light and fewer vehicles.
Never pick flowers or break branches; it is a protected sanctuary.
Stay at the road edge on stops; do not walk into the forest without a guide.
Carry binoculars for birds and a light rain jacket for afternoon showers.
Flying drones here is not allowed without permission.

experiences.title: Rhododendron photo stops on the Yumthang road
experiences.summary: Ask your driver for two or three short stops between Lachung and Yumthang, where the road runs through the thickest rhododendron forest. Early light, empty roads and full bloom are worth more than an hour at the crowded meadow.
body: On the drive from Lachung to Yumthang, the road climbs through the sanctuary for much of its 24 km. In bloom season, whole slopes are coloured, and individual trees can be covered in flowers. Most vehicles race up to the meadow. If you ask your driver politely the evening before, they will usually stop for a few minutes at good spots on the way up or back.

Choose stops on straight stretches with room to pull over, not bends. Step to the forest side, away from traffic. Use a mid-range zoom to frame single trees against the fir forest, and look for colour differences: deep red, pink, white, cream and yellow species often grow within a few hundred metres of each other.

Rhododendrons are protected here. Do not pull branches down for close-ups, pick flowers or walk into the undergrowth. Many species are slow-growing, and the sanctuary exists precisely because of past cutting. A long lens or phone zoom gives you the close-up without damage.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see rhododendrons in North Sikkim
faqs.a: Usually from about the third week of April to late May in the Shingba sanctuary and around Yumthang, with lower slopes earlier and higher slopes later. Exact timing shifts with each year's weather. The first half of May is the safest bet for a full bloom.

faqs.q: Can I walk inside Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary
faqs.a: Not freely. Tourists see the sanctuary from the Yumthang road and short roadside stops. Walking into the forest off the road is discouraged and may require forest department permission and a guide. Some treks pass through the area with special permits through registered operators.

faqs.q: How many rhododendron species are in Shingba
faqs.a: Sources differ: some say over 24 species, others around 40. The variation reflects different surveys and what counts as a distinct species. Either way, it is one of the richest rhododendron areas in India, and you will see several different colours and forms in one morning.

experiences.title: Early birding in the Shingba forest
experiences.summary: With a private car and a local guide, the forest edge on the Yumthang road can be good for high-altitude birds. Go at first light, keep stops short and quiet, and accept that sightings are a matter of luck.
body: Shingba's Wikipedia entry records the wood snipe and the hoary-throated barwing among its birds. Forests at this height in Sikkim also hold species such as the blood pheasant, Sikkim's state bird, and the Himalayan monal, though seeing them depends on season, disturbance and luck. Smaller birds such as tits, warblers and rosefinches are easier.

Birding needs a private car, because group vehicles will not wait. Leave Lachung at first light, stop where the forest is thickest and the road quiet, and scan the edges and clearings. A local guide from Lachung who knows the calls will make a big difference; ask your hotel to find one.

Keep voices down, do not use playback near nesting birds and never chase pheasants into the undergrowth. Be back on the main schedule in time to visit Yumthang and leave Lachung so that you cross the Toong checkpost by 4 pm if you are heading south.

faqs.q: What birds can I see in Shingba sanctuary
faqs.a: Recorded species include the wood snipe and hoary-throated barwing. Forests at this height in Sikkim also hold the blood pheasant, Sikkim's state bird, and the Himalayan monal, along with tits, warblers, rosefinches and others. Sightings depend on season, time of day and luck.

faqs.q: Is the blood pheasant found in North Sikkim
faqs.a: Yes. The blood pheasant is Sikkim's state bird and lives in high-altitude forests and scrub across the state, including the upper Lachung and Lachen valleys. It is shy and most often seen early in the morning near forest edges, sometimes in small groups.

faqs.q: Can I go birding on a group package
faqs.a: Only casually. Group vehicles keep to a fixed schedule and will not wait for birds. For serious birding, hire a private car from Gangtok or Lachung and a local guide, and leave at first light. Discuss your plan with your operator when booking.

experiences.title: Find Sikkim's state tree
experiences.summary: A simple game for families on the Yumthang road: spot Rhododendron niveum, Sikkim's state tree, by its tight balls of magenta flowers and white-felted leaves. It teaches children to look closely at a forest.
body: Rhododendron niveum is a small evergreen tree or large shrub, 2–6 m tall, with leathery leaves. Young leaves are covered with white felt, which stays on the underside; that is what the Latin name niveum, snowy, refers to. Its flowers are intense magenta to lilac, held together in a compact ball above the leaves.

It grows between about 2,600 and 3,500 m, which matches the lower part of the Shingba sanctuary. Give children the description before you leave Lachung and ask them to spot it from the car. Your driver may know it as the state flower tree; many people in Sikkim do.

When you find one, stop if it is safe and look without touching. Turn a fallen leaf over to see the white underside, but do not pull leaves from the tree. Compare it with the red tree rhododendrons and paler species nearby. It is a five-minute lesson in why this forest is protected.

faqs.q: What is the state tree of Sikkim
faqs.a: The state tree of Sikkim is Rhododendron niveum, a rhododendron native to Sikkim, Bhutan and southern Tibet. It has magenta to lilac flowers in compact heads and leaves with a white felt underneath. It grows between about 2,600 and 3,500 m in places like the Lachung valley.

faqs.q: Where can I see Rhododendron niveum
faqs.a: In the Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary and elsewhere in the Lachung and Lachen valleys at about 2,600–3,500 m, and in other high forests of Sikkim. It flowers in spring, mainly April and May. Ask your driver or a local guide to point it out on the Yumthang road.

faqs.q: Can I take rhododendron flowers home
faqs.a: No. Picking flowers or breaking branches in the sanctuary is not allowed, and taking plants out of protected areas is illegal. Photograph them instead. Seed and nursery plants of some species are sold legally elsewhere if you want to grow them.

experiences.title: The sanctuary in autumn gold
experiences.summary: Outside flower season, Shingba is still worth looking at. In late October and November, birch and other broadleaf trees turn gold and rust among the dark firs, under the clearest skies of the year.
body: Most people think of Shingba only in May, but autumn has its own colour. From late October, birch and other deciduous trees among the firs turn yellow and russet, and rhododendron leaves show their deep green against them. The sky is usually at its clearest in November.

Autumn is also quieter. Puja week brings crowds, but in the weeks after Diwali there are far fewer vehicles on the Yumthang road. Mornings are frosty, around or below freezing, and the light low and clear. It is a good time for photography and for anyone who wants the forest to themselves.

Dress for cold: thermals, a down jacket, gloves and a cap. Rhododendron buds for next spring are already set on the branches; leave them alone. If snow comes early, the forest turns white quickly, and the road may be cleared only partway.

faqs.q: Is Shingba worth visiting outside spring
faqs.a: Yes, as part of the Yumthang drive. In autumn the broadleaf trees turn gold among the firs under clear skies; in winter the forest is often snowbound. You will not see rhododendron flowers, but you will see a protected high forest in a different season, often with fewer people.

faqs.q: When does autumn colour peak near Lachung
faqs.a: Usually from the last week of October to mid-November, depending on when the cold sets in. Larches, birches and maples turn first on higher slopes. By late November many trees are bare. November skies are generally the clearest of the year.

faqs.q: Is the Yumthang road open in November
faqs.a: Usually yes, if no early heavy snow falls, and the sanctuary and Yumthang are visited daily. Zero Point may close from mid-December. Landslide damage from the monsoon is often repaired by then, but conditions change. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where is Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary
faqs.a: It is in the upper Lachung valley of North Sikkim, between Lachung and Yumthang, covering about 43 square km at roughly 3,000–3,700 m. The road from Lachung to Yumthang runs through it. It is part of the Mangan district and the wider Sacred Himalayan Landscape.

faqs.q: When was Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary established
faqs.a: It was established in 1984 to protect the rhododendron forests of the Lachung valley. It covers about 43 square km. Yumthang valley lies within or beside it, and tourists see it on the Yumthang drive with their Lachung permit.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate ticket for Shingba sanctuary
faqs.a: Not as a standard tourist. Your Lachung–Yumthang permit, arranged by a registered operator, covers driving through the sanctuary to Yumthang. Research visits, treks or filming may need separate forest department permission. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the best month for Shingba rhododendrons
faqs.a: May, with late April a close second. Lower slopes flower first, from mid to late April, and the bloom moves uphill into late May. Weather shifts the peak by a week or two each year. Book Lachung hotels early for these weeks.

faqs.q: Is Shingba the same as Yumthang Valley
faqs.a: Not exactly. Shingba is the rhododendron sanctuary covering the forested slopes of the upper Lachung valley; Yumthang is the meadow valley at its upper end, at 3,564 m. Many sources describe Yumthang as home to the sanctuary. On the ground you pass through both on one drive.

faqs.q: Can I trek in Shingba sanctuary
faqs.a: Not on a standard tourist permit. Some longer treks, such as routes linking Yumthang and the Lachen side, pass through the area but need special permits, registered operators and guides. For most visitors, roadside stops on the Yumthang drive are the way to see it.

faqs.q: How many rhododendron species are found in Sikkim
faqs.a: Sikkim is known for a large number of rhododendron species, and the Shingba sanctuary alone is said to hold between about 24 and 40. Counts vary between surveys. The state flower of Sikkim is the noble dendrobium orchid; its state tree is Rhododendron niveum.

faqs.q: Can foreigners visit Shingba sanctuary
faqs.a: Yes, as part of a Lachung–Yumthang trip on a Restricted Area Permit arranged through an approved operator, in a group of at least two. Foreign nationals can usually visit Lachung and Yumthang. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Shingba sanctuary open in the monsoon
faqs.a: The sanctuary itself is not closed, but tourist permits for Lachung and Yumthang are often suspended during the monsoon, from June to September, because of landslides. In 2025 permits resumed on 8 September. Check current status before you travel.
